Side Effects: Common side effects may include reduced appetite, difficulty sleeping, coughing, flu-like symptoms, or pain, redness, and swelling at the injection site. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks. However, it is important to note that this medication may increase the risk of cancer. Your doctor will closely monitor your condition through laboratory and medical tests. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States or Canada and experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. Precautions: Before using teduglutide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and Medical Tests: Tests such as colonoscopy, fecal occult blood testing, lipase/amylase levels, and liver function tests should be conducted before starting this medication and periodically while using it. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze it or store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Teduglutide, commonly sold under the brand name Gattex, is used by patients with Short Bowel Syndrome (SBS) who require intravenous (IV) nutrition and fluids. It may help reduce the amount of IV nutrition needed. Teduglutide is similar to a natural hormone in the body called GLP-2. How to Use: Read the Medication Guide and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist before starting teduglutide and each time you get a refill. Consult your healthcare professional on how to prepare and use this medication. Inject this medication under the skin as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. The injection is typically administered in the thigh, abdomen, or upper arm. Do not shake the vial. Before use, inspect the product for particles or discoloration. If either is present, do not use the liquid. Before injecting each dose, clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol. Rotate the injection site each time to minimize skin injury. To reduce bruising, avoid rubbing the injection site after the injection. Use this medication regularly to gain the most benefit.
